title: Rogers’s theorem for acceptable numberings

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §6.2 Definition 6.10 and Theorem 6.11, printed/PDF pp.33–34, with the translated-index repair MARKS-CT-07; §5.2 matching argument reused through the existing Myhill entry

summary: Replace two behavior-preserving program compilers by a computable permutation, using self-reference to keep translated names distinct.
abstract: Two program languages may compute the same partial functions while giving their programs different numerical names. Effective translation in both directions does not make the supplied compilers inverse or injective. Rogers’s theorem shows that a stronger translation can nevertheless be constructed: a computable permutation of all program names preserving every returned value and every divergence. Padding gives an injective compiler into the standard numbering. For the other direction, self-referential programs test whether their translated names have appeared before; a collision forces a special undefined case that supplies a fresh name by a second probe. Iterating this argument gives injective translations in both directions, and the effective matching construction turns them into a bijection with a computable inverse. The labels preserved by this construction are whole partial functions, whose equality need not be decidable.
